steps.name: Notice the forms in a short text
Sentences of your own with AI feedback

pilotRules.speaking: Record 60–90 seconds. Hide the model before the first take. One specific AI correction, then record again straight away.
pilotRules.writing: 30 minutes, 120–150 words, instant AI feedback and revise-and-retry. A few days later a new speaking prompt without the phrase bank.
pilotRules.conversation: 15 minutes recommended; 3–4 turns with the AI partner on the week's theme, grammar and featured words. Feedback after the exchange, then one turn retried.
pilotRules.extensiveInput: About 60 minutes a week of graded B1 listening or reading with transcripts or captions, tagged to the week's theme; 40 minutes minimum; up to 5 personal words.
pilotRules.progression: No fixed days or deadlines. The next week opens when speaking, writing and either listening or reading are done.
pilotRules.level: Adults and older teenagers (16+) at secure B1. Adult contexts: work, flat-sharing, plans and travel. Judge control and clarity, not the number of forms used.
pilotRules.grammarClinic: Only syllabus B1 basics: present simple and continuous, articles, quantifiers, prepositions, subject–verb agreement and verb forms. Every Light point is taught in its own week, not moved to the clinic.

conversationRules.levelAndTurns: The partner speaks at B1 in one- or two-sentence turns and asks one follow-up per turn. Ends after 3–4 learner turns, or earlier on request.
conversationRules.errors: No interruption or mid-conversation corrections; natural recasts only, e.g. 'Oh, you've lived there since May?'
conversationRules.feedback: After the exchange: up to three corrections prioritising the week's grammar, one featured word used well or one that would have fitted, then one turn retried.
conversationRules.labelledAsAi: The partner and its feedback are always labelled as AI; learners can dispute feedback with 'I think this is right'.
conversationRules.accent: Feedback covers grammar, vocabulary and clarity. A Spanish or regional accent is never an error; misrecognised words are not grammar mistakes.
conversationRules.safety: Stays on the week's theme, declines romantic, sexual, harmful or personal-data topics, never asks for an address or phone number, suitable for ages 16–17, report button on every exchange, transcripts kept under the privacy policy.

weeks.title: A change you got used to
weeks.canDo: Tell a story about a change: set the scene, sequence events and connect them to now.

grammar.main: narrative tenses; present perfect vs past simple.
grammar.light: used to / would; present perfect continuous.
grammar.authoringNote: Would for past habits is not normally used in negatives, questions or states; accept used to or the past simple there, and don't flag the past simple where used to is possible. Contrast result ('I've made a few friends') and activity ('I've been running').

notice.text: Three years ago, I moved to Bristol for work. I had never lived abroad before, so the first months were hard. One morning, while I was waiting for the bus, I started chatting to a neighbour. She invited me to a book club. We used to meet every Thursday, and we would always argue about the ending! I have lived here for three years now, and I've been going to that club ever since.

items.prompt: "I had never lived abroad before." Had the speaker lived abroad before moving to Bristol?
items.reason: The past perfect describes the situation before the move.

items.prompt: "While I was waiting for the bus, I started chatting." Which action was in the background?
items.reason: The past continuous sets the scene; the past simple is the event.

items.prompt: "I have lived here for three years." Does the speaker still live in Bristol?
items.reason: The present perfect connects the past to now.

items.prompt: I ___ to Bristol three years ago.
items.reason: "Three years ago" is a finished time.

items.prompt: I ___ a lot of new friends since then.
items.reason: "Since then" means up to now.

items.prompt: When I arrived at the station, the train ___.
items.reason: It left before I arrived.

items.prompt: I ___ dinner when my phone rang.
items.reason: A longer action interrupted by a short one.

items.prompt: ___ you ever ___ in another country?
items.reason: "Ever" asks about life experience up to now.

items.prompt: She ___ her job last month and is now looking for a new one.
items.reason: "Last month" is a finished time.

items.prompt: While we ___ (drive) to the coast, it started to rain.
items.reason: Background action.

items.prompt: By the time I got to the party, most people ___ (go) home.
items.reason: They left before I arrived.

items.prompt: I ___ (know) Maria since we were at school.
items.reason: Up to now with "since"; know is not used in the continuous.

items.prompt: Last summer I ___ (spend) two weeks in Scotland.
items.reason: Finished time.

items.prompt: She was tired because she ___ (not sleep) the night before.
items.reason: Earlier than the moment she was tired.

items.prompt: I have moved to Leeds in 2023.
items.reason: "In 2023" is a finished time, so use the past simple.

items.prompt: When I got home, my flatmate already cooked dinner.
items.key: When I got home, my flatmate had already cooked dinner.
items.reason: Cooking happened before I got home.

items.prompt: I was knowing her for years before we worked together.
items.key: I had known her for years before we worked together.
items.reason: Know is a state verb, and this happened before the other past event.

items.prompt: I started learning English in 2020. I'm still learning it. (since)
accepted: I have been learning English since 2020.
items.reason: An activity that continues up to now.

items.prompt: First the film started. Then we arrived. (When ... already)
items.key: When we arrived, the film had already started.
accepted: The film had already started when we arrived.
items.reason: The past perfect shows which happened first.

items.prompt: I was walking home. I saw an accident. (While)
items.key: While I was walking home, I saw an accident.
accepted: I saw an accident while I was walking home.
items.reason: Background plus event.

items.prompt: When I was a child, we ___ in a small flat.
items.reason: Live is a state, so would is not possible.

items.prompt: Every summer, my grandfather ___ us fishing.
items.reason: A repeated action in the past.

items.prompt: I'm tired because I ___ all morning.
items.reason: An activity up to now with a result you can see.

items.prompt: Tell me about something you used to do as a child that you don't do now.
items.key: Any correct sentence with used to or would
items.reason: AI checks the form and gives one correction.

items.prompt: What has changed in your life since you started your current job or studies?
items.key: Any correct sentence with the present perfect and since
items.reason: AI checks the form and gives one correction.

items.prompt: I usually ___ to work, but this week I'm working from home.
items.reason: A usual habit uses the present simple.

items.prompt: She's ___ engineer.
items.reason: Use an before a vowel sound.

items.prompt: We ___ (watch) TV when the lights went out.
items.reason: Background action interrupted.

items.prompt: I ___ (never / see) snow until I moved to Canada.
items.reason: Before another past event.

items.prompt: She ___ (work) here since 2019.
items.reason: Up to now with "since"; both forms are correct.

speaking.prompt: Tell me about a change in your life. What was life like before? What changed, what was difficult, what helped, and what is different now?
speaking.cueCard: Before · The change · What was hard · What helped · Now
phraseBank: In my old town, I used to... / we would...
The biggest challenge I faced was...
It took me a while to get used to...
When I look back on..., I...
speaking.model: > When I moved to a new city last year, I didn't know anyone. In my old town, I used to see my friends every weekend, and we would often cook together on Sunday evenings. So the biggest challenge I faced was meeting people outside work. It took me a few weeks to get used to spending my evenings alone. One evening, while I was walking home, I saw a poster for a running group. I'd never run with a group before, so I was nervous at the first session, but I gradually got to know the other runners. Since then, I've made a few friends, and the city feels more like home. I've been running with the group for about six months now. When I look back on those first few weeks, I'm really glad I went to that first session.
speaking.onTarget: covers all five cue points; uses the past perfect or past continuous at least once and the present perfect at least once; uses two featured items.
speaking.correctionPriority: 1) past simple vs present perfect with time words (last year, since); 2) would with states (would live); 3) the -ing form after get used to.

shadowingChunks.chunk: It took me a few weeks to get used to it.
shadowingChunks.listenFor: used to sounds like "yoosta"; stress on weeks and used

shadowingChunks.chunk: I'd never run with a group before.
shadowingChunks.listenFor: the short I'd; stress on never, run and group

shadowingChunks.chunk: Since then, I've made a few friends.
shadowingChunks.listenFor: I've is short; made_a links together

conversation.title: catching up with an old friend

turns.partner: It's been ages! What's changed since I last saw you?
turns.learner: Name a change (past simple, present perfect)
turns.followUp: Oh really? When did that happen?

turns.partner: Wow. Was it hard at first?
turns.learner: Describe a challenge (past continuous or past perfect; face a challenge)
Say what is different now (present perfect, since then, present perfect continuous)
turns.followUp: How long have you been doing that?

turns.partner: Do you miss anything about your old life?
turns.followUp: What did you use to do at weekends?

conversation.closingLine: It's great to hear you're doing well. Let's not leave it so long next time!

speaking.delayedRecall: Tell me about a new routine that felt strange at first. What helped it feel normal?
speaking.b2Stretch: explain why the change mattered and how you feel about it now, without the cue card.

writing.prompt: Write a personal narrative about a change. Set the scene, use since then or eventually to move the story on, and close with one sentence about how things are now.
writing.delayedRecall: Tell me about a new routine that felt strange at first. What helped it feel normal?

conversation.openingLine: It's been ages! What's changed since I last saw you?

core.example: I had to adapt to living abroad.
Moving to Leeds was a turning point in my life.
I faced several challenges while I was studying abroad.
It took me a month to get used to living alone.
When I look back on my first year abroad, I remember the people I met.
I've never regretted leaving my old job.
My English gradually improved while I was living in York.
Travelling alone was a memorable experience.

collocations.example: I made a big decision about my future.
I took a risk and applied for a job abroad.
I decided to make a change and cycle to work.
I've kept in touch with my old school friends.
I've been making good progress since September.
I took up photography after I moved.

families.card: decision is productive on the collocation card; decisive and indecisive recognition only

vocabulary.note: Teach get used to + noun or -ing for B1 production; contrast used to + infinitive on the same card. Keep adapt to as guided B2.

linkers.example: Eventually, I got used to it.
I moved in September. Since then, I've made some good friends.

weeks.title: A goal and the next step
weeks.canDo: Describe an intention, name an arrangement, say what happens next and what you'll do if plans change.

grammar.authoringNote: 'I will see my dentist tomorrow' is grammatical; don't flag it just because the visit is booked. Accept will or going to for predictions with present evidence. Conditional labels are teaching aids: accept natural variants such as 'when' in a zero conditional.

notice.text: My goal this year is to get a better job. I'm going to update my CV this weekend, and I'm meeting a careers adviser on Tuesday. The course I want starts on 3 March. I think it'll be hard, but when I finish it, I'll apply for jobs in marketing. If I don't get an interview, I'll ask for feedback. And if I had more time, I'd study full-time!

items.prompt: "I'm meeting a careers adviser on Tuesday." Is this an arrangement already made, or a decision made now?
items.reason: The present continuous is used for fixed arrangements.

items.prompt: "When I finish it, I'll apply." Is finishing the course in the present or the future?
items.reason: After when, use the present simple for the future.

items.prompt: "If I had more time, I'd study full-time." Does the speaker have more time?
items.reason: The second conditional describes an imagined situation.

items.prompt: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
items.reason: A prediction based on what you can see now.

items.prompt: I ___ lunch with my sister tomorrow. We've booked a table.
items.reason: A fixed arrangement.

items.prompt: My flight ___ at 6 a.m., so I need to leave home at 4.
items.reason: Timetables use the present simple.

items.prompt: A: I've left my wallet at home. B: Don't worry, I ___ for the coffees.
items.reason: An offer or decision made while speaking.

items.prompt: I'll call you as soon as I ___ home.
items.reason: After as soon as, use the present simple for the future.

items.prompt: I ___ start my own business one day. That's my plan.
items.reason: An intention with no fixed arrangement yet.

items.prompt: We ___ (move) to Valencia next month. We've already signed the contract.
items.reason: A fixed arrangement.

items.prompt: I'm sure you ___ (enjoy) the course.
items.reason: A prediction based on opinion.

items.prompt: Before I ___ (start) my new job, I'm going to take a holiday.
items.reason: After before, use the present simple for the future.

items.prompt: I ___ (not / come) to the meeting on Friday. I've got a dentist's appointment.
items.reason: A fixed arrangement.

items.prompt: Wait, I ___ (help) you carry that.
items.reason: An offer made while speaking.

items.prompt: I'll tell you when I will know the results.
items.key: I'll tell you when I know the results.
items.reason: After when, use the present simple for the future.

items.prompt: I can't come on Saturday. I will visit my parents. We arranged it last week.
items.reason: It was arranged, so use the present continuous.

items.prompt: We're go to the cinema tonight.
items.key: We're going to the cinema tonight.
items.reason: The present continuous needs the -ing form.

items.prompt: My plan: find a new flat. (going to)
items.key: I'm going to find a new flat.
items.reason: An intention.

items.prompt: Finish work, then phone you. (as soon as)
items.key: I'll phone you as soon as I finish work.
accepted: As soon as I finish work, I'll phone you.
items.reason: Will in the main clause, present simple after as soon as.

items.prompt: Meeting with Ana, Thursday 3 p.m., booked. (present continuous)
items.key: I'm meeting Ana on Thursday at 3 p.m.
items.reason: A fixed arrangement.

items.prompt: If you heat ice, it ___.
items.reason: Zero conditional: always true.

items.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll stay at home.
items.reason: First conditional: present simple after if.

items.prompt: If I ___ you, I'd take the job.
items.reason: Second conditional: an imagined situation.

items.prompt: Tell me one plan you have for next month and one thing you've already arranged.
items.key: Correct sentences with going to and the present continuous
items.reason: AI checks the form and gives one correction.

items.prompt: What would you do if you had a free year with no work or study?
items.reason: AI checks the form and gives one correction.

items.prompt: I ___ in this city since 2021.
items.reason: Up to now with since.

items.prompt: When I was young, I ___ love cartoons.
items.reason: Love is a state, so would is not possible.

items.prompt: I ___ (see) the doctor at 10 tomorrow. It's booked.
items.reason: A fixed arrangement.

items.prompt: I think it ___ (be) sunny at the weekend.
items.reason: A prediction based on opinion.

items.prompt: Call me after you ___ (land).
items.reason: After after, use the present simple for the future.

speaking.prompt: Tell me about a goal you have. What have you already arranged, what will you do when that step is complete, and what will you do if the plan changes?
speaking.cueCard: My goal · Already arranged · When it's done... · If it doesn't work out...
phraseBank: If it doesn't work out, I'll...
speaking.model: > My goal is to start a career in design. I intend to take a short course this spring, and I'm meeting someone from the college on Thursday. I'm looking forward to seeing some of the students' work. A friend who did the course has offered to help me choose a project. I think it'll be hard work, but it'll be worth it. When I finish the course, I'll apply for a few junior roles and use my project to show what I can do. If I don't get a place this spring, I'll take an evening class instead. And if I had more free time, I'd study full-time, but I need to keep working for now.
speaking.onTarget: covers all four cue points; uses at least two different future forms correctly; uses a first or second conditional; uses two featured items.
speaking.correctionPriority: 1) will after when, as soon as or if (when I will finish); 2) going to vs present continuous for arrangements; 3) look forward to + -ing.

shadowingChunks.chunk: I'm looking forward to seeing their work.
shadowingChunks.listenFor: to is weak ("tuh"); stress on look, for and see

shadowingChunks.chunk: When I finish the course, I'll apply.
shadowingChunks.listenFor: the short I'll; a small pause after course

shadowingChunks.chunk: If I had more free time, I'd study full-time.
shadowingChunks.listenFor: the short I'd; rising tone after time, falling at the end

weeks.title: Agree on house rules
weeks.canDo: Say what is required, forbidden, optional or possible, ask and give permission, and offer advice.

grammar.main: modals of obligation, advice, ability, permission.
grammar.authoringNote: For a specific past success use was able to or managed to, not could; couldn't works for a specific failure. Keep this contrast as a B2 note, not a scored item.

notice.text: Welcome to the flat! A few things: we have to put the bins out on Thursdays, and you mustn't smoke inside. You don't have to join us for dinner, but you're always welcome. You can use the washing machine until 10 p.m. If anything breaks, you should ask Tom. He can fix almost anything! Could you tell me when you're arriving? Apart from that, just make yourself at home.

items.prompt: "You don't have to join us for dinner." Is dinner required, optional or not allowed?
items.reason: Don't have to means it isn't necessary.

items.prompt: "You mustn't smoke inside." Is smoking inside optional or not allowed?
items.reason: Mustn't means it is forbidden.

items.prompt: "He can fix almost anything." Is this about ability or permission?
items.reason: Here can describes what Tom is able to do.

items.prompt: You ___ wear a seatbelt in a car. It's the law.
items.reason: A rule, not just advice.

items.prompt: It's a free museum, so you ___ pay.
items.reason: Paying isn't necessary, but it isn't forbidden.

items.prompt: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.
items.reason: Advice, not a rule.

items.prompt: ___ I use your phone? Mine's dead.
items.reason: Asking for permission.

items.prompt: When I was ten, I ___ swim very well.
items.reason: General ability in the past.

items.prompt: Passengers ___ use their phones during take-off.
items.reason: It is forbidden.

items.prompt: I ___ (have to / work) late tomorrow, so I can't come.
items.reason: A requirement.

items.prompt: You ___ (not / have to / bring) anything. We've got plenty of food.
items.reason: Not necessary.

items.prompt: Sorry, I ___ (can / not / hear) you. Can you speak up?
items.reason: Ability, negative.

items.prompt: I think you ___ (should / talk) to your manager about it.
items.reason: Advice.

items.prompt: ___ I ___ (can / borrow) your charger?
items.reason: A permission question: can before the subject.

items.prompt: You must to show your ticket.
items.reason: Modals are followed by the verb without to.

items.prompt: She can speaks three languages.
items.reason: No -s after a modal.

items.prompt: Do I can leave early today?
items.reason: Modals make questions without do.

items.prompt: It isn't necessary to book a table. (don't have to)
items.key: You don't have to book a table.
accepted: We don't have to book a table.
items.reason: Not necessary.

items.prompt: Smoking is not allowed here. (mustn't)
items.reason: Forbidden.

items.prompt: Is it OK if I sit here? (Could)
items.reason: A polite permission question.

items.prompt: Put the words in order: What time / you / usually / do / get home?
items.key: What time do you usually get home?
items.reason: Auxiliary before the subject in questions.

items.prompt: ___ the bins out on Thursdays?
items.reason: Who is the subject, so no do.

items.prompt: The flat is small. ___, it's very close to the station.
items.reason: It introduces a contrasting point.

items.prompt: Tell a new flatmate one thing they have to do, one thing they mustn't do and one thing they don't have to do.
items.key: Correct sentences with have to, mustn't and don't have to
items.reason: AI checks the form and gives one correction.

items.prompt: Ask your new flatmate two questions about their routine.
items.reason: AI checks word order and gives one correction.

items.prompt: I'll text you when I ___ at the station.
items.reason: After when, use the present simple for the future.

speaking.prompt: A new flatmate arrives tomorrow. Record a welcome: explain one shared responsibility, one rule and one optional routine, give one piece of advice, and end with a question for them.
speaking.cueCard: A shared job · A rule · Something optional · Advice · A question for them
phraseBank: If you need..., just ask politely
speaking.model: > Welcome to the flat! There are a few things you need to know. We have to clean up after cooking, and we mustn't leave the cooker on when we go out. You don't have to cook for everyone, but we usually eat together on Fridays. You can use the washing machine until ten. The neighbours can hear it through the wall, so if you need it later, please ask them politely first. I couldn't cook at all when I moved in, so don't worry if you're still learning. I think we should arrange a cleaning rota around our work hours. Apart from that, there's no fixed routine. We all get on with each other really well, so if you're not sure about something, just ask. What time do you usually get home, by the way?
speaking.onTarget: covers all five cue points; uses have to, mustn't and don't have to correctly at least once between them; gives advice with should; ends with a correctly formed question; uses two featured items.
speaking.correctionPriority: 1) mustn't vs don't have to; 2) to after a modal (must to); 3) question word order.

weeks.title: Give a short visitor guide
weeks.canDo: Describe customs and past facts with the passive, identify places and compare them.

grammar.authoringNote: Use a guide-card cue such as 'Market hall / build / 1890' in controlled practice. In free speech accept natural active wording; don't require a set number of passives.

notice.text: Toledo is one of the oldest cities in Spain. Work on its cathedral was started in 1226, and today the city is visited by thousands of tourists every year. Marzipan is made in local convents and bakeries, and it is sold in shops all over the old town. The best time to go is spring, when it's quieter than in summer. There's a viewpoint where you can see the whole city.

steps.exercise: Notice: listen to and read a short text, tap the target forms
Check the meaning: short questions about what the form means
Complete: verb or prompt in brackets

steps.markedBy: App, with AI checking other correct answers

steps.exercise: Use it yourself: two sentences about your own life, spoken or typed
steps.markedBy: AI, instant feedback and one retry

practice.extraPractice: Each week has 3 extra items. A learner who scores below 60% on steps 3-4 gets them before moving on; a learner who scores 90% or more on steps 3-4 skips step 6.
practice.feedback: Every item has a one-line reason, shown straight after the answer. Wrong answers become review cards. In steps 6 and 8 the AI accepts any correct answer that uses the target form, not only the key.
practice.itemFormat: Each item has an id, a step, a target (Main, Light or Review), the prompt, the options where there are any, the key, accepted variants, and the reason.

items.prompt: "Marzipan is made in local convents and bakeries." What is the sentence mainly about?
items.reason: The passive puts the focus on the thing, not the person doing the action.

items.prompt: "Work on its cathedral was started in 1226." Present or past?
items.reason: Was + past participle is the past simple passive.

items.prompt: "There's a viewpoint where you can see the whole city." What does where refer to?
items.reason: Where introduces information about a place.

items.prompt: English ___ in many countries.
items.reason: The language is the focus; people speak it.

items.prompt: This bridge ___ in 1890.
items.reason: Past time, passive.

items.prompt: The rooms ___ every morning.
items.reason: Rooms don't clean; someone cleans them.

items.prompt: The thieves ___ by the police yesterday.
items.reason: The police did the action; the thieves received it.

items.prompt: My bike ___ last night!
items.reason: Someone stole it; we don't know who.

items.prompt: Paella ___ in the pan it is cooked in.
items.reason: Someone serves the paella.

items.prompt: The festival ___ (hold) every August.
items.reason: Present passive; hold, held, held.

items.prompt: The letters ___ (deliver) yesterday afternoon.
items.reason: Past passive, plural subject.

items.prompt: These photos ___ (take) by my grandfather in 1975.
items.reason: Past passive; take, took, taken.

items.prompt: Breakfast ___ (not / include) in the price.
items.reason: Present passive, negative.

items.prompt: Where ___ your car ___ (make)?
items.reason: Past passive question.

items.prompt: The museum was build in 1920.
items.reason: The passive needs the past participle.

items.prompt: The windows are clean every week.
items.key: The windows are cleaned every week.
items.reason: Someone cleans them: use the past participle.

items.prompt: The castle visited by thousands of tourists every year.
items.key: The castle is visited by thousands of tourists every year.
items.reason: The passive needs be.

items.prompt: They built the castle in the 12th century. (passive)
items.key: The castle was built in the 12th century.
items.reason: The castle is the focus.

items.prompt: People grow oranges in this region. (passive)
items.key: Oranges are grown in this region.
items.reason: "People" adds nothing, so leave it out.

items.prompt: Someone stole my wallet on the train. (passive)
items.key: My wallet was stolen on the train.
items.reason: We don't know who did it.

items.prompt: That's the restaurant ___ we had our first date.
items.reason: Where for a place followed by a full clause.

items.prompt: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
items.reason: Who for people.

items.prompt: The old town is ___ the new town.
items.reason: Comparing two places.

items.reason: Second conditional.

items.prompt: Coffee ___ (grow) in Colombia.

speaking.prompt: Record a short guide for someone visiting your town for the first time. Include a regular event or custom, one fact about the past, one comparison, and a recommendation.
speaking.cueCard: An event or custom · A fact about the past · A comparison · My recommendation
phraseBank: It's a local tradition / custom to...
It's one of the ...est places in...
speaking.model: > If you visit this town, start at the market hall. It was built in 1890, and the food market is held there every Saturday. It's a local tradition, and you can try food from nearby farms. It's the busiest place in town on a Saturday morning, so I'd set off early. There's also a local custom that surprises visitors: most shops are closed on Wednesday afternoons, so plan your shopping for another day. Afterwards, take a walk by the river. It's quieter than the centre, and it's the spot where I go to relax. The town isn't a famous destination, but it's one of the friendliest places I know.
speaking.onTarget: covers all four cue points; uses at least one present passive and one past passive correctly; uses a comparative or superlative; uses two featured items. Do not require a set number of passives.
speaking.correctionPriority: 1) be + past participle (was build, is visit); 2) irregular participles (held, built, taken); 3) comparative forms (more quiet, the most big).

productionNotes: Model answers: four recordings (one per week), British English, natural pace (about 130-150 words a minute), with transcripts. Use at least two different speakers across the four weeks and record each speaker's accent in the audio metadata.
Shadowing chunks: 12 short clips cut from the model recordings, each at normal speed and at 0.8 speed, with transcripts.

Conversation partner: a British synthetic voice labelled as AI, with a 0.9-speed option and live captions; scripts follow the turn maps above, and the partner may vary its wording but stays on the week's theme and level.
Delayed-recall prompts: text and audio, scheduled 3-5 days after the speaking task.
Checkpoint 1 prompt: text and audio; never shown before the checkpoint.
Safety: conversation transcripts are moderated in both directions, kept under the privacy policy, and every exchange has a report button.
Review before launch: a second teacher checks every model answer, cue card and turn map against the grammar plan and vocabulary list, and listens to every recording.
reviewChecklist: [ ] Each wrong option is clearly wrong in its context (no second correct answer).
[ ] Accepted variants cover the common correct answers for rewrite and complete items, including contractions.
[ ] Each reason is one short line a B1 learner can understand.
[ ] Notice-text facts are correct (Week 4: Toledo cathedral begun in 1226; marzipan made in local convents and bakeries).
[ ] Vocabulary in the prompts stays at B1 or uses that week's featured words.
[ ] Timing checked with 3-5 pilot learners: the set takes 18-22 minutes.
[ ] Items converted to the app's JSON curriculum format and passed the schema validation.
[ ] Checkpoint 1 items are written separately, not copied from this bank, so the checkpoint tests learning rather than memory of the practice items.
